queue.title: Crouch-look camera pan ($307D: B+Down / B+Up, 1 px/frame, edge-gated)
queue.note: Verified missing 2026-10-13: $0F71's FIRST call, and the port neither implements it nor flags it. Gated on sSceneState == 0 and (sMarioOnGround | sMarioOnObject); hKeysHeld $82 (B+Down) pans camY +1/frame while sMarioScreenY >= $20 and not (edge bit3 and camY_lo >= $C0); $42 (B+Up) pans camY -1/frame while sMarioScreenY < $70 and not (edge bit2 and camY_lo < $49). Uses the same sScreenEdgeMap as the follow, so it needs the extracted table too. The capture field named `pan` is sCameraPanTimer ($A2B3), which $307D never writes - it is NOT this feature's flag. The real evidence that the gate was blind: across the original 16 captures (~49k frames) no frame holds B+Down or B+Up while grounded. KEY LAYOUT (ReadJoypad $1FD2, verified 2026-10-13): hKeysHeld = directions in bits 4-7 (bit7 Down, bit6 Up, bit5 Left, bit4 Right) and actions in bits 0-3 (bit1 B, bit0 A, bit2 Select, bit3 Start) - so $82 is exactly Down+B, $42 exactly Up+B, and $08 (the $287E START wait) is Start. Because `cp` is exact, Select or Start held CANCELS the pan; the port cannot express those bits yet, so this becomes a live dependency of the pause item (pause_and_palette_flash) - when a START bit lands, the pan gate must include it. DONE 2026-10-13: CameraSim::crouch_pan (13 unit tests, cargo test 84) plus captures/crouch_pan1.json (508 records, $05E4-hook-sampled). That capture holds B+Down for 79 grounded frames and B+Up for 80, with 41 camy +1 steps, 41 -1 steps and 75 guard-blocked frames (camy 406-448); the port replays it ALL-ZERO on all 507 compared frames, so both pan arms and both guards match the console. Added to the README gate list.

queue.title: sy98 model vs the real stale sMarioScreenY ($A23B) register
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (the up-lock latch test) + the 18-capture gate, measured byte-identical with the fix
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-14, by measurement rather than by changing the model first (which is what this item asked for).
WHAT WAS WRONG: the `$0D97` tail of `$0C7D` is `ldh a,[$FFC0] / ld [sPrevMarioY],a` - it latches the LIVE Mario Y. The up-lock warp (`home.asm:1782-1790`) writes `$FFC0 = 0` and then falls into that same tail, so on the warp frame the ROM latches 0 while the port latched the value the body entered with, leaving the next frame's `dv = $FFC0 - sPrevMarioY` short by the pre-warp low byte on every frame after an up transition. Fixed: `CameraSim::step` now ends with `self.prev_mario_y_lo = sim.y as u8` (the live byte) instead of the entry snapshot `my_lo`.
MEASURED FIRST (the item's own recommendation): a temporary probe tracked both latches frame by frame. Body-warps DO fire - 8 of the 18 captures (traj10, traj11, traj12, traj13, traj14, traj16, death3, screen_transition1), one each - and the `dv` branch classification (zero / < $80 / >= $80) differs on 0 frames in all 18. The decisive A/B is the gate itself, because the camera moves by dv's MAGNITUDE and not just its branch: with the live latch the 18-capture gate is byte-identical to the pre-fix run. So the fix is fidelity, not a level-1 behaviour change - which also matches the note's own reading that the register's readers are the two lock rows the transition ends never straddle with a stale value.
TEST: one new camera test (`the_up_lock_warp_latches_the_warped_y_not_the_entry_value`) drives the real warp arm (camera on the `$48` lock row with edge bit2, Mario's Y lo $C0 against a latch of 0 for the `>= $80` up branch and `sy98 = $1A < $1B`) and asserts the warp, `sim.y = 0`, and the latch reading 0 rather than $C0. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix model ($C0) and pass with it, so it pins the behaviour rather than describing it.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE - the other half of the conflation: `prev_mario_y_lo` is still one field for two ROM bytes. The movement role now correctly models `sPrevMarioY` ($A20C); the `$C0`/`$48` hard-edge reads want the draw's `sMarioScreenY` ($A23B), modelled as `sy98 = prev_mario_y_lo - cam_y_lo + $62`. Splitting it into two fields would be unverifiable by any capture (the two bytes differ only on frames where the register is not consulted: the first frame after `$0F2A`, transition frames, parked frames) and the note's recommendation was to keep the sy98 model, which this item's measurements now support. If a future capture shows a lock-row divergence at a transition end, that is the first thing to split.

queue.title: Autoscroll camera path ($0DAF) is unmodelled
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (6 tests) + a play-mode smoke run; capture-less by construction - see autoscroll_capture
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-13, implemented straight from the pinned description. `CameraSim::step` now mirrors `$0B2A`'s dispatcher: `if self.auto_scroll != 0 { self.run_autoscroll(sim) } else { <the $0B5E right chain + the $0BE5 left chain> }`, and the vertical follow below is untouched because `$0DAF` itself jumps to `$0C7D`. `run_autoscroll` does the three things the ROM does and nothing else: the right-edge trigger (`>= $B0` where `$0B5E` tests `== $B0`; and below `sMarioScreenX = $A1` it `ret`s outright instead of falling through to the scroll), the one-pixel-per-two-frames scroll (`ldh a,[$FF97] / and $01 / ret nz` - the port's `sim.phase & 1`, the same parity the down-transition dither reads), and `sScrollLeftEnabled` cleared with `sMapScrollFlags` bit 4 set. It never applies the player-speed latches, never reads either enable, and has no ±1 park nudge, no $FF99 pull-back, no left edge lock and no left transition. The carry is masked to four bits (`& $0FFF`). `$0C76`'s scroll-delta clear is skipped by the ROM's jump; the port derives d_r/d_l from `x_sub` every frame and keeps no persistent deltas, so there is nothing to clear here (noted in the code).
VERIFIED: 6 new unit tests - the even/odd cadence with the left-enable clear and bit 4, the latches and both enables being ignored (`x_sub = 40` still moves exactly 1 px), the high-byte wrap ($0FFF + 1 -> $0000), the right-edge arm's three outcomes ($B0 + sx $A5 -> transition 1; $B0 + sx $70 -> nothing at all; $AF -> scroll), and the left chain being skipped ($50 column + sx $05 -> no transition, Mario not warped, the autoscroll px instead), plus the shared vertical follow still running. cargo test 97. The 18-capture gate is byte-identical - expected, since no gated level is autoscroll - which is also why this path has NO capture coverage: the stale 'that path is not modelled' note in both loops is now a capture-coverage note, so an autoscroll level added to the gate would flag itself. Runtime smoke check: `--level 19 --play` (level20, autoscroll) runs 15s on the new dispatcher without incident. Filed `autoscroll_capture` for the real thing.

queue.title: START pause + the BGP/OBP0 $E7/$93 flash (16 frames each - a 32-frame cycle off $FF97 bit 4)
queue.verification_gate: cargo test + manual --play check of ENTER/BACKSPACE (no capture can carry START)
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-13 - core plus the --play wiring. CAVEAT: the interactive path could not be driven in this environment (no key-injection tool: xdotool/ydotool/wtype and grim/scrot/import are all missing), so the window path is verified by construction and by the core tests, not by a capture or a screenshot.
PINNED ROM FACTS: pause is game state $FF9B = 8, not a separate handler - entry stub $273E (home.asm:5181-5194, called at the in-level frame tail from home.asm:818 and the dead branch at 827), handler $2756 (home.asm:5196-5239) via the $08 table entry at home.asm:303. The flash is bit 4 of the global counter $FF97 read EVERY frame ($E7 when clear, $93 when set, home.asm:5197-5201) - a 32-frame cycle off the counter, with no timer and no reload value - and the same byte goes to sBGPalette AND sOAMPalette1 (home.asm:5204-5206); sOAMPalette2/OBP1 is never written. Entry needs hKeysPressed == $08 exactly and sScreenTransition == 0, and the in-level loop zeroes both key bytes while sFadeTimer != 0. Resume is on any frame with the START press bit: it restores the three sLevel* copies ($A80F-$A811) and sets $FF9B = 4. SELECT ($04) with sLevelProgressFlags bit 7 set quits through $FF9B = 20 -> $14. Music pauses via sSoundMode = 1/2 (a held jingle), not sMusicRequest.
PORTED: PlayerKeys gained start/select (the pan's exact-match test now includes both); PlayerSim gained `paused` (the $FF9B = 8 model) and `frame_counter` (the full $FF97 byte - the port kept only `phase`, its low 3 bits, which cannot see bit 4), plus pause_enter/pause_exit/pause_flash/pause_select_exit. --play maps ENTER to START and BACKSPACE to SELECT, tracks both press edges like hKeysPressed, and freezes sim.step/cam.step/obj.step on a paused frame exactly as a fade does - the freeze is read at entry, so the frame START lands on still runs its object pass, because $273E sits at the frame tail. The flash is threaded into the renderer as a BG-palette override plus a per-frame SpriteCtx.obp0 write, so BG and OBJ0 flash together while OBP1 does not; unpaused frames restore the manifest's OBJ0. FLAGGED, not invented: sSoundMode 1/2 (no sound-mode state in the port), sPauseState ($A23D, write-only in the ROM), sMarioDead = 2, sFastMusic; and the ROM's `hKeysPressed == $08` is modelled as 'the START edge on a frame with no fade or transition', since ENTER is not a gameplay key.
TESTS: 4 - the 16/16 flash cadence off bit 4 including both boundaries, enter/exit, the SELECT branch's bit-7 gate with its exit marker, and respawn clearing the pause. cargo test 88; the 18-capture gate is unchanged (no capture carries START, so the replay path passes start:false and the frozen flag stays clear).

queue.title: Scene system: sSceneMap-nonzero levels run a scene at the transition finish (sSceneState = $F0 + the bank-5 script VM $20A4 + the bank-2 $8D9C boss/template set + $8E6C)
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (scene.rs: 9 VM tests incl. the all-32-scripts parse; camera.rs: the $0F0B latch) - capture-less by construction, see scene_capture
queue.note:
SLICE 1 DONE 2026-10-14: the scene map, the script table and the VM for non-boss scenes. THREE OF THIS ITEM'S PINNED CLAIMS WERE WRONG and are corrected here - everything below this paragraph assumed them, so read this first.
CORRECTIONS (verified against baserom.gb + the dispatch chain): (a) $6x takes NO operand byte, not 1: $25AF's first instruction is `ld a,[hli]` with HL already on the opcode, so it eats the opcode byte itself and the nibble IS the tileset index. Reading it as one operand makes all seven level-entry scripts pick tileset 0. (b) $Bx takes THREE operands, not 2 (`B2 1E 00 6C FF` parses as opcode+3+$FF, and 2 or 4 do not fit). (c) $8E6C does NOT use a $10 stride with overlapping images: `e = ((e + $10) & $F0) + 5` moves exactly +$20, so each 18-byte image sits at slot+5 inside its own 32-byte slot, with no overlap (confirmed by sObject0Def $AD05 vs sObject1Def $AD25 and the spawner's `ld de,$0020`). Also: $3A14 loads bank 25 ($19), not 19 (the bank-2 section is merely NAMED bank19), and the `$FFCC-$FFCF` values the $4x direction streamers write feed $0969/$0A35 - the VRAM BG-window streamers - so they are invisible to this port, which renders from the resident layout.
THE VERDICT THAT BOUNDED THIS SLICE: for a scene that is only `$4x` + `$FF` (the level-03 pair), $3C94/$8D9C/$8DFD/$8E6C are NOT reached at all - $3C94 has exactly one caller, $0EB0, gated on `sSceneState & $0F`, and only the $2x opcode ever sets that (to 15). So no BossFightPhase key data, no `sObjectDefCount` and no $8DA9 driver is needed for these scenes; the normal $8000 engine keeps running.
WHAT LANDED: `levelNN.scene.bin` extraction (32 levels, independently re-derived, zero mismatches); runtime wiring of CameraSim::scene_map + the header's initial sSceneState + the new scene flag bytes; `cargo test` coverage of the $0F0B latch against level 3's real cells; and a new `sml2-core/src/scene.rs` holding the extracted bank-5 `$4125` table (32 scripts, `extracted/scenes/script_table.bin`) and the `$20A4` VM: one script byte per frame, the per-class operand lengths, `$FF` END with the `$21EE` epilogue (latch sSceneTransitionFlag -> sSceneTransitionLatch, zero sSceneId/sSceneIdHi/flag/done), the `$4x` teleport (operand high nibble -> the camera's AND Mario's Y page $FFC9/$FFC1, low nibble -> their X page $FFCB/$FFC3, low bytes untouched, then sSceneTransitionFlag = 1), `$8x` arming sBossDefeated = $F0 | nibble (the whole of level 25's `81 FF`/`82 FF` scenes), and the unhandled-nibble hang reproduced as a no-advance stall. The entry prologue's frame wait is modelled, so the first byte runs on the frame after the latch, and the VM is driven once per frame at the end of the in-level pass in BOTH loops (home.asm:274 runs $20A4 after the state pass).
STRONGEST EVIDENCE: all 32 retail scripts parse into whole instructions landing exactly on their `$FF` using the confirmed length table (a test asserts this), which is what caught (a) above.
WHAT REMAINS, filed as scene_boss_scripts: `$2x` (scene_state = 15 + the 96-frame fade - the arm that reaches the bank-2 scene load), `$3x` (camera/Mario Y add-or-set), `$6x` (tileset swap), `$Bx`/`$0x` (VRAM block transfers), the palette writers `$1x`/`$5x`/`$Ax` (absent from every retail script, so unimplemented insurance), then $8D9C/$8DFD/$8E6C and the `$8DA9` alternate driver. Reachable in retail: the six boss arenas (scene ids 11-16 and 19) and the castle's id 27 (`20 FF`). The gate capture is filed as scene_capture.

PARTIAL 2026-10-14 - the foundation landed and was verified independently; the VM and the scene-load branch are still pending.
(1) EXTRACTION. sml2-extract now writes levelNN.scene.bin (48 bytes) for all 32 levels from the level header's [$4002] pointer + (layout_index & $0F)*48, through the SAME code path as the edge map so the two files cannot drift apart. Verified from scratch against baserom.gb: for all 32 levels both maps match an independent Python read (32/32, zero mismatches), 14 levels have a nonzero scene map (matches the claim), and level03's ids are exactly {6,7} - at row0/Xhi4 and row1/Xhi5, i.e. entries 4 and 21 of the (Yhi & $0F)*16 + (Xhi & $0F) index - so the first-slice target is confirmed. Also measured: NO level has a nonzero header +18 high nibble, so the initial sSceneState is 0 everywhere and the 'level starts inside a scene' path is unreachable in this ROM.
(2) RUNTIME WIRING. Both loops load the map into CameraSim::scene_map and seed cam.scene_state from that header nibble ($0609), so $0F0B's scene_lookup now latches real scene ids instead of always 0; a missing or short map prints a note rather than silently latching 0 (the same rule the edge table has). Two new camera tests pin the latch against level 3's REAL cells (id 7 at index 4, id 6 at index 21), the $0F masking of the Xhi nibble, and a cell past the 3-row map reading 0 instead of out of range. Gate byte-identical and note-free (level 1's map is all zeros); cargo test 99.
(3) REMAINING in this item: the $0EB0 `sSceneState & $0F` branch (state 240 + the $3C94 -> bank 2 $8D9C body with its two clears, $8DFD's def records and $8E6C's 18-byte slot images), the bank-5 script VM $20A4 (the $4125 table, the fetch loop, the opcode operand lengths, $FF END, $21E8/$2728 halt) with the $4x opcode that sets the screen hi bytes, and the alternate per-frame driver $8DA9 while `sSceneState & $F0 != 0`. ROM research for those was dispatched as deleg_c19cd322 and is not in this commit.
CROSS-ITEM NOTE: the autoscroll levels have scenes too - level20 (the first autoscroll level) carries scene id 13 at its own cell, so `autoscroll_capture` and this item overlap.
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-10-13 (this item, and DESIGN.md, claimed 'state 240' and 'bank-1 $3C94'). 240 is stored into sSceneState (= $F0), NOT $FF9B: the $FF9B jump table ends at $23 (home.asm:330) so 240 could never index it. $3C94 is a bank-0 trampoline to bank 2 $8D9C. Real chain: a hard-edge trigger in $0B2A sets sScreenTransition and calls $0F0B, which latches sSceneId from sSceneMap; when the scroll completes $0EB0 (home.asm:2009-2050) tests sSceneState & $0F and, if nonzero, sets sSceneState = $F0 then calls $3C94 -> $8D9C. Missing from the port: (1) the bank-5 script VM $20A4 (one byte per frame, halt between bytes, 32-entry dw table at $4125 indexed by sSceneId, opcode operand lengths 7/1/0/2/1/0/1/0/0/3 for $0x/$1x/$2x/$3x/$4x/$5x/$6x/$8x/$Ax/$Bx, $FF = END at $21EE); (2) the $0EB0 sSceneState & $0F branch in camera.rs's finish_transition (whose comment says 'bank-1', also wrong); (3) the bank-2 $8D9C path (it does not load VRAM: it clears $AF00-$AFFF and sObjectTable $AD00, then $8DFD builds sObjectDefIndex/sObjectDefCount/sObjectDefSprite, then $8E6C writes 18-byte slot images at a literal $10 stride into $AD25+ - consecutive images OVERLAP by 2 bytes, which is what the ROM arithmetic does, so reproduce it literally); (4) the alternate per-frame driver $8DA9 that REPLACES the normal $8000 engine while sSceneState & $F0 != 0 (selected at home.asm:830-842), with its $92DF anim table, $9048/$505B extents and $3A14 -> bank 19 $6000. sSceneMap extraction mirrors the edge map but from the pointer at [bank:$4002] (home.asm:572-604) -> levelNN.scene.bin; the port's camera.rs scene_lookup already implements the $0F0B index ((MarioYhi & $0F)*16 + (MarioXhi & $0F)) but scene_map is never filled by the runtime, so scene_id is always 0 today. 14 of 32 levels have a nonzero scene map; level 1 is all zeros (re-verified from baserom.gb), which is why no capture touches this. Cleanest first slice: level 3 (level_id 2), whose two scenes are $06 = 40 03 FF and $07 = 40 16 FF - pure 'transition to screen (Y,X)' with no tileset/VRAM/boss/fade work; then level 8 (scenes $01/$02). Full detail in the delegation transcript deleg_52e18705 task-4.

queue.title: Scene slice 2: the $2x boss-arena scripts, the bank-2 scene load ($8D9C/$8DFD/$8E6C) and the $8DA9 driver
queue.verification_gate: cargo test + a boss-arena capture (level 8s ids 11-16 / level 25s id 27)
queue.note: The half of the scene system that needs the bank-2 machinery. Entry points: `$2x` (sets sSceneState = 15, sFadeTimerHigh = 1/sFadeTimerLow = 96, clears sTileAnimConfig and the star timers -- this is the ONLY writer that makes `$0EB0`'s `sSceneState & $0F` test pass, i.e. the only way `$3C94` is ever called), `$3x` (2 operands: camera Y then Mario Y, absolute when the opcode low nibble is 0 and a 16-bit add otherwise, targeting $FFC8/$FFC9 and $FFC0/$FFC1), `$6x` (NO operand: the nibble is the tileset index into $268B/$2699 -- see the corrections in scene_system), `$Bx` (3 operands, VRAM transfer) and `$0x` (7 operands, VRAM transfer). Reachable retail scripts: ids 11-16 and 19 in levels 8/10/13/16/17/20 (the arena pattern `6x 20 30 yy zz 40 nn FF` -- $6x tileset, $2x arm, $3x offsets, $4x cell, END) and id 27 in level 25 (`20 FF`, the castle). Then the called-into chain: $3C94 -> bank 2 $4D9C = four calls ($3A28 -> bank 3 $EC40 clears $AF00-$AFFF; $3A00 -> bank 3 $EC31 clears $AD00-$AEFF; $8DFD builds sObjectDefIndex = sBossFightPhase + b (b: level 5->0, 9->1, $0D->2, $10->3, $13->4, $17->5, else 6), sTimerReload = 80, and reads a 3-byte record (count, hits=6, sprite) through the 9-POINTER table at $4E3F via $904E -- the record table itself has no stride arithmetic; $8E6C copies an 18-byte slot image to $AD05 and then sObjectDefCount more of them at +$20 each through the tables at $4E9A/$4EAC), plus the alternate per-frame driver $8DA9 (selected by $0652 when `sSceneState & $F0 != 0`, REPLACING the whole $8000 engine that frame) with its deps $81A7/$81BD/$92DF (the 29-entry per-object behaviour table via rst $28)/$3A14 (bank 25)/$9048 -> $81DB + the $505B descriptor table. Careful: the port's own `finish_transition` scene branch is currently a documented non-branch, and `$2x` setting sSceneState = 15 (low nibble) is NOT the same as the high-nibble park -- model both or neither, never half.

queue.title: No capture reaches a scene: level 1s scene map is all zeros
queue.verification_gate: a PyBoy capture on a level with a nonzero scene map, crossing the edge under a scene cell
queue.note: The scene VM is unit-pinned against the real script bytes (all 32 scripts parse into whole instructions ending exactly on $FF) and the wiring is exercised every frame by the 18-capture gate, but no capture ever LATCHES a scene, so the latched path has never run against the console. Measured 2026-10-14: level 1s scene map is all 48 bytes zero, and the 14 levels that do have scene cells span 22 distinct scene ids -- so any of those levels can produce the capture, and the cheapest is the one already used for the level-3 analysis: level03 (level_id 2, `--level 2`) whose cells (Yhi 0, Xhi 4) -> id 7 (`40 16 FF`) and (Yhi 1, Xhi 5) -> id 6 (`40 03 FF`) teleport Mario AND the camera to cells (1,6) and (0,3) respectively. A capture would need to cross a right/left/up/down screen edge while standing on one of those two cells; the harness would then show the teleport (Mario/cam X and Y pages jumping) one frame after the latch, and the END epilogue clearing sSceneId. NOTE the port has no capture fields for scene state, so the capture is only read through the existing x/y/camx/camy/frame/edge checks -- which is enough to catch the teleport and the transition frame, but NOT the flag bytes.

queue.title: Golden coins (sGoldenCoin1-6 $A84D-$A865) and the map-side tally ($307BC / $30884)
queue.note: CONFIRMED with one caveat, 2026-10-13. An exhaustive scan of baserom.gb (every ld [$A84x],a / ld hl,$A84x / ld a,[$A84x] / 16-bit pointer pair / set 7,(hl) site for the six addresses) finds NO in-level writer: the six bytes are written only by (a) $27AF at home.asm:5321-5327 (game over, zeroes all six), (b) the level-clear chain at main.asm:16661-16672 with $304F1 giving levels 5/9/13/16/19/23 the offsets 5/9/$1D/$17/$11/$0E, (c) the map hand-off $3EEF0 (main.asm:24089-24124) via $650E for the six coin nodes, and (d) the SRAM load. So the port's 'no in-level writer' note holds. CAVEAT: the corollary 'c is always 0' is NOT a general invariant - it holds only for a save with no coin-level progress; once any of the six coin levels is completed the corresponding byte is set and $27AF's BCD subtract is nonzero. Also: sGoldenCoinCount never feeds the level-clear tally (that is +1 BCD per newly cleared level, coin-independent); the only tally/coin interaction is the game-over subtraction.

queue.title: No gate covers --play: the mode with no capture is where the edge-map bug lived
queue.note:
The 2026-10-13 camera bug was invisible because the replay path injected the console's $FF98 and only --play had to derive it. The edge check now covers the derivation, but the class remains: any field the harness seeds from a capture's frame 0 (limit, autoscroll, easy, ff0, uphase, pcx) is unverified in play mode. Options: drive --play from a capture's inputs headlessly, or seed both modes from the level header and check the header against the captures' frame 0.
PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-13: the two loops now share one `build_contact` helper, so the `MarioContact` fields can no longer drift per mode - that closed `star_high`, `invincibility` and `on_object` (the play loop had passed defaults for all three) and, separately, the missing `on_ground_cleared` write-back in the play loop. What remains structurally: the play loop still has its own copy of the per-frame write-back list (mario_y_adjust / on_ground_cleared / on_ground_obj / stomp_jump / stomp_bounce / pending_item / mario_dead) with no test that the two lists match, and `pan` / `scene_state` / `flutter` are 0 in both paths because nothing drives sCameraPanTimer / sSceneState / sFlutterTimer. The cheapest real fix is to extract the whole per-frame step (sim.step + camera + object pass + write-backs) into one function both loops call, then assert its effects from a test - that would put a capture-less mode under `cargo test`.

queue.title: PlayerSim::on_ground_obj is never set true, so every gate that reads sMarioOnObject is inert
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (measured gate-neutral: 0 on-object frames in all 18 captures)
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-13. The runtime now copies the object engine's result into the sim at both write-back sites: `sim.on_ground_obj = obj.on_object` (the ROM's $2D7D clears sMarioOnObject at the top of the pass and $2DF7/$2E1A raises it to 255 when Mario stands on an `sObjectType & $23` bit5 object; a pass the frame loop skips, i.e. pipe travel, leaves the byte alone - which is what objects.rs's `!travelling` guard around `collide` reproduces). Three readers were dead, all now live: $129F's landing arm (the flag short-circuits to $1378, which forces sMarioOnGround = 255 and clears sPipeTravelDirection, so the floor probe never runs), the $5375/$53FE walk-cycle frame test, and $307D's `(sMarioOnGround | sMarioOnObject)` pan gate. Found in the same sweep: the PLAY loop's write-back list was missing `on_ground_cleared` outright, so --play disagreed with every capture on that too. Both loops now build their MarioContact through one `build_contact` helper (the play loop had been passing defaults for star_high, invincibility and on_object - three more silent play/replay divergences; see infra_play_parity_harness).
MEASURED, not assumed: a temporary probe over all 18 captures shows the on-object arm firing on 0 frames, and the gate stayed byte-identical after the write-back landed. Tests: 3 added - the $1378 short-circuit with a collision_tile sentinel proving the probe is skipped, its control (the same blank layout without the flag launches a running Mario off the ledge: hvel $C0 -> vvel 27 once the rest of the frame has run, hvel $80 -> no launch at all), and the walk-pose frame test with sMarioOnGround clear. cargo test 91.
FOLLOW-UP, filed as obj_on_object_capture: no LEVEL-1 capture can ever cover this. Dumping every contact that passes the $2EF5 box test in all 18 captures gives exactly 39 contacts - 38 of type $4E and 1 of $56 - and both have `ty & $23 == $02`, i.e. bit5 CLEAR. The types that merely reach the $2EDD type gate ($44, $56, $85, $86, $87) are all rejected by the box test, and every one of those also has bit5 clear in `& $23` ($44 -> $00, $56 -> $02, $85 -> $01, $86 -> $02, $87 -> $03). Level 1 has no stand-on object at all, and the $2E1A arm additionally needs a gentle contact (y_delta < $0C), which the falling stomp takes first.
